# ToFaRev review

Review complete within the supplied scope.

Source inspection only; PR code, tests, and benchmarks were not executed.

No supported findings were reported within the reviewed scope.


## Coverage

- Static, source-only review&#58; all 31 changed paths were read via /`source/diff.txt` in full, cross-checked against /source/head and /source/base files; tests were not executed and no cluster environment was available, so the three new test files were assessed by inspection only.
- [`cmd/root.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/cmd/root.go#L1-L1) verified&#58; `checkLabRuntimeCommandSupport` runs in `preRunFn` before topology parsing; `graphRendersFromTopologyFile` reuses the pre-existing `labRuntimeFlagWasSet` helper; the `labRuntimeUnsupportedFlags` contract now covers graph --node-filter.
- [`core/config.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/core/config.go#L1-L1) `LoadTopologyNodes` verified&#58; for lab runtimes it builds nodes/links without initializing container runtimes &#40;early break in the `nodeRuntimes` loop&#41;; for local runtimes it is a no-op because `NewContainerLab` already parsed the topology.
- labruntime/clabernetes verified&#58; every exported cluster-touching method &#40;Deploy, Destroy, Inspect, List, `LabExists`, Exec, `StreamEvents`, Plan, Save, Start/Stop/Restart&#41; calls connect&#40;&#41;; Validate and Manifests are intentionally offline; the `clientLoader.once` pattern makes concurrent connect safe.
- `events.go/state.go/iface_stats.go` verified&#58; bounded channels with ctx-aware non-blocking sends, `newestPod` selection and `podsByNode` guards are correct; the `noShell` cache is keyed by pod name so replaced pods are re-probed; interface sampling powers state events with stats piggybacking, a documented tradeoff.
- [`cmd/inspect.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/cmd/inspect.go#L1-L1) and [`types/types.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/types/types.go#L1-L1) verified&#58; nil-embedded &#42;`LabRuntimeWorkload` omits its fields from JSON, matching the docker-record assertions in [`cmd/labruntime_gaps_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/cmd/labruntime_gaps_test.go#L1-L1); `ShortID` now equals the unique &#60;namespace&#62;/&#60;lab&#62;/&#60;node&#62; ID per [`core/labruntime_gaps_test.go`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/core/labruntime_gaps_test.go#L1-L1).
- Docs verified against implementation&#58; [`destroy.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/docs/cmd/destroy.md#L1-L1) &#40;claim retention without --cleanup&#41;, [`events.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/docs/cmd/events.md#L1-L1) &#40;namespace/lab scoping; Docker/Podman ignoring lab selection matches the unfiltered local stream path&#41;, [`graph.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/docs/cmd/graph.md#L1-L1) &#40;topology-file-only modes&#41;, `inspect/index.md` &#40;new JSON fields&#41;, and [`runtime.md`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/docs/manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#L1-L1) lines 353/381/772 document that deploy --reconfigure deletes persistent node storage.
- [`schemas/clab.schema.json`](https://github.com/srl-labs/containerlab/blob/091e76f302da47a75bf351543c9e82bc63b0ed11/schemas/clab.schema.json#L1-L1) requires no change&#58; the Cleanup/Retain persistence semantics belong to the c9s CRD domain, not the clab topology schema.

1: ---
2: description: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring code to avoid overcomplication, make surgical changes, surface assumptions, and define verifiable success criteria.
3: alwaysApply: true
4: ---
5: 
6: # Karpathy behavioral guidelines
7: 
8: Behavioral guidelines to reduce common LLM coding mistakes. Merge with project-specific instructions as needed.
9: 
10: **Tradeoff:** These guidelines bias toward caution over speed. For trivial tasks, use judgment.
11: 
12: ## 1. Think Before Coding
13: 
14: **Don't assume. Don't hide confusion. Surface tradeoffs.**
15: 
16: Before implementing:
17: 
18: - State your assumptions explicitly. If uncertain, ask.
19: - If multiple interpretations exist, present them - don't pick silently.
20: - If a simpler approach exists, say so. Push back when warranted.
21: - If something is unclear, stop. Name what's confusing. Ask.
22: 
23: ## 2. Simplicity First
24: 
25: **Minimum code that solves the problem. Nothing speculative.**
26: 
27: - No features beyond what was asked.
28: - No abstractions for single-use code.
29: - No "flexibility" or "configurability" that wasn't requested.
30: - No error handling for impossible scenarios.
31: - If you write 200 lines and it could be 50, rewrite it.
32: 
33: Ask yourself: "Would a senior engineer say this is overcomplicated?" If yes, simplify.
34: 
35: ## 3. Surgical Changes
36: 
37: **Touch only what you must. Clean up only your own mess.**
38: 
39: When editing existing code:
40: 
41: - Don't "improve" adjacent code, comments, or formatting.
42: - Don't refactor things that aren't broken.
43: - Match existing style, even if you'd do it differently.
44: - If you notice unrelated dead code, mention it - don't delete it.
45: 
46: When your changes create orphans:
47: 
48: - Remove imports/variables/functions that YOUR changes made unused.
49: - Don't remove pre-existing dead code unless asked.
50: 
51: The test: Every changed line should trace directly to the user's request.
52: 
53: ## 4. Goal-Driven Execution
54: 
55: **Define success criteria. Loop until verified.**
56: 
57: Transform tasks into verifiable goals:
58: 
59: - "Add validation" → "Write tests for invalid inputs, then make them pass"
60: - "Fix the bug" → "Write a test that reproduces it, then make it pass"
61: - "Refactor X" → "Ensure tests pass before and after"
62: 
63: For multi-step tasks, state a brief plan:
64: 
65: ```
66: 1. [Step] → verify: [check]
67: 2. [Step] → verify: [check]
68: 3. [Step] → verify: [check]
69: ```
70: 
71: Strong success criteria let you loop independently. Weak criteria ("make it work") require constant clarification.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: **These guidelines are working if:** fewer unnecessary changes in diffs, fewer rewrites due to overcomplication, and clarifying questions come before implementation rather than after mistakes.

(End of file - total 75 lines)
</content>

<content>
1: ---
2: description: Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode. Always pick the simplest solution that works.
3: globs:
4: alwaysApply: true
5: ---
6: 
7: # Ponytail, lazy senior dev mode
8: 
9: You are a lazy senior developer. Lazy means efficient, not careless. The best code is the code never written.
10: 
11: Before writing any code, stop at the first rung that holds:
12: 
13: 1. Does this need to be built at all? (YAGNI)
14: 2. Does it already exist in this codebase? Reuse the helper, util, or pattern that's already here, don't re-write it.
15: 3. Does the standard library already do this? Use it.
16: 4. Does a native platform feature cover it? Use it.
17: 5. Does an already-installed dependency solve it? Use it.
18: 6. Can this be one line? Make it one line.
19: 7. Only then: write the minimum code that works.
20: 
21: The ladder runs after you understand the problem, not instead of it: read the task and the code it touches, trace the real flow end to end, then climb.
22: 
23: Bug fix = root cause, not symptom: a report names a symptom. Grep every caller of the function you touch and fix the shared function once — one guard there is a smaller diff than one per caller, and patching only the path the ticket names leaves a sibling caller still broken.
24: 
25: Rules:
26: 
27: - No abstractions that weren't explicitly requested.
28: - No new dependency if it can be avoided.
29: - No boilerplate nobody asked for.
30: - Deletion over addition. Boring over clever. Fewest files possible.
31: - Shortest working diff wins, but only once you understand the problem. The smallest change in the wrong place isn't lazy, it's a second bug.
32: - Question complex requests: "Do you actually need X, or does Y cover it?"
33: - Pick the edge-case-correct option when two stdlib approaches are the same size, lazy means less code, not the flimsier algorithm.
34: - Mark deliberate simplifications that cut a real corner with a known ceiling (global lock, O(n²) scan, naive heuristic) with a `ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling and upgrade path.
35: 
36: Not lazy about: understanding the problem (read it fully and trace the real flow before picking a rung, a small diff you don't understand is just laziness dressed up as efficiency), input validation at trust boundaries, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, the calibration real hardware needs (the platform is never the spec ideal, a clock drifts, a sensor reads off), anything explicitly requested. Lazy code without its check is unfinished: non-trivial logic leaves ONE runnable check behind, the smallest thing that fails if the logic breaks (an assert-based demo/self-check or one small test file; no frameworks, no fixtures). Trivial one-liners need no test.

(End of file - total 36 lines)
</content>

559: +	t.Parallel()
560: +
561: +	c := &CLab{Config: &Config{Name: "lab1"}, TopoPaths: &clabtypes.TopoPaths{}}
562: +	ports := []clablabruntime.ExposedPort{{Port: 22, ExposePort: 22, Protocol: "tcp"}}

573: +		},

576: +	if container.ID != "c9s-lab1/lab1/r1" || container.ShortID != container.ID {
577: +		t.Fatalf("ID = %q, ShortID = %q; want the unique <namespace>/<lab>/<node> id",
578: +			container.ID, container.ShortID)

582: +		w.Container != "node-r1-x" || w.NodeUID != "uid-1" ||
583: +		w.LoadBalancerAddress != "192.0.2.10" || len(w.ExposedPorts) != 1 {

657:  
658:  The local `--cleanup | -c` flag instructs containerlab to remove the lab directory and all its content.
659:  
660:  Without this flag present, containerlab will keep the lab directory and all files inside of it.
661:  
662: +With `--runtime c9s`, `--cleanup` also deletes the lab's persistent node storage (the PersistentVolumeClaims holding saved device configuration) and then the lab namespace. A plain destroy keeps the claims, so the next deploy of the lab boots from the saved configuration. See [device state persistence](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#device-state-persistence).
663: +
664:  Refer to the [configuration artifacts](../manual/conf-artifacts.md) page to get more information on the lab directory contents.
665:  
666:  #### graceful
667:  
668:  To make containerlab attempt a graceful shutdown of the running containers, add the `--graceful` flag to destroy cmd. Without it, containers will be removed forcefully without even attempting to stop them.

853:  ## Events
854:  
855: -The c9s runtime can stream Node, Topology, pod, and interface-stat events:
856: +The c9s runtime can stream Node, Topology, pod, interface state and
857: +interface-stat events:
858:

860:  containerlab --runtime c9s events --format json
861:  containerlab --runtime c9s events --initial-state
862:  containerlab --runtime c9s events --interface-stats --format json
863: +containerlab --runtime c9s events --name clos --format json
864: +containerlab --runtime c9s --namespace team-a events --format json
865:  ```
866:  
867:  For c9s, events do not come from Docker events on the outer host. Containerlab
868:  watches:
869:  
870:  - c9s `Node` resources carrying `c9s.run/topologyOwner`
871:  - `Topology` resources
872:  - Pods labeled with `c9s.run/topologyOwner`
873:  
874: +What the stream covers:
875: +
876: +| Invocation | Scope |
877: +|---|---|
878: +| `events` | every namespace |
879: +| `--namespace <ns> events` or `CLAB_KUBE_NAMESPACE=<ns>` | the labs in `<ns>` |
880: +| `events -t <topo>` or `events --name <lab>` | that lab, in its namespace (`c9s-<lab>`, or the namespace override) |
881: +
882: +An identity whose RBAC only covers one namespace needs one of the scoped forms;
883: +watching every namespace requires cluster-wide `list` and `watch`.
884: +
885:  With `--initial-state`, the stream starts with synthetic events for the current
886: -c9s node state and then continues with live watches.
887: +c9s node state and the state of every interface, then continues with live
888: +watches.
889: +
890: +Container events use the node's `<namespace>/<lab>/<node>` ID as actor, the
891: +`container_id` inspect reports.
892: +
893: +### Interface events
894: +
895: +Containerlab samples the interfaces of every running node by exec into its
896: +device container. One exec per node and interval reads `/proc/net/dev` and
897: +`/sys/class/net/*/operstate` (with index, MTU, MAC address, flags and alias).
898: +All containers of a device pod share one network namespace, so the samples
899: +cover the node's pod interfaces.
900: +
901: +Interface state events are always streamed. They use the same schema as the
902: +interface events of the local runtimes, with the operational state as action:
903: +
904: +```json
905: +{
906: +  "timestamp": "2026-10-27T10:15:02.123456789Z",
907: +  "type": "interface",
908: +  "action": "down",
909: +  "actor_id": "c9s-clos/clos/srl1",
910: +  "actor_name": "clos-srl1",
911: +  "actor_full_id": "srl1-7d9c6b5f4-x2k8p",
912: +  "attributes": {
913: +    "ifname": "e1-1",
914: +    "state": "lowerlayerdown",
915: +    "index": "7",
916: +    "mtu": "9232",
917: +    "mac": "aa:c1:ab:5e:2f:01",
918: +    "lab": "clos",
919: +    "node": "srl1",

2096: +	lines := strings.Split(data, "\n")

2099: +	for _, line := range lines {

2104: +
2105: +		state := c9sIfaceState{

2118: +		}
2119: +		if state.OperState == "" {
2120: +			state.OperState = "unknown"
2121: +		}
2122: +
2123: +		states = append(states, state)
2124: +	}
2125: +
2126: +	return states

2227: +// handlePersistentClaims deletes the lab's persistent node storage on a destroy with Cleanup.
2228: +// Without Cleanup it keeps the claims the lab retained and returns their number.
2229: +func (r *Runtime) handlePersistentClaims(
2230: +	ctx context.Context,
2231: +	req clablabruntime.DestroyRequest,
2232: +	namespace string,
2233: +) (int, error) {
2234: +	claims := r.kubeClient.CoreV1().PersistentVolumeClaims(namespace)
2235: +	selector := labels.Set{labelTopologyOwner: req.Name}.String()
2236: +
2237: +	list, err := claims.List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{LabelSelector: selector})
2238: +	if err != nil {
2239: +		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to list persistent claims of c9s lab %s/%s: %w",
2240: +			namespace, req.Name, err)
2241: +	}
2242: +
2243: +	if !req.Cleanup {
2244: +		retained := 0
2245: +		for idx := range list.Items {
2246: +			// Claims owned by a Node are garbage-collected with it.
2247: +			if len(list.Items[idx].OwnerReferences) == 0 {
2248: +				retained++
2249: +			}
2250: +		}
2251: +		if retained != 0 {
2252: +			log.Info(
2253: +				"Keeping persistent node storage of C9s lab; destroy with --cleanup to delete it",
2254: +				"name", req.Name,
2255: +				"namespace", namespace,
2256: +				"claims", retained,
2257: +			)
2258: +		}
2259: +
2260: +		return retained, nil
2261: +	}
2262: +
2263: +	if len(list.Items) == 0 {
2264: +		return 0, nil
2265: +	}
2266: +
2267: +	log.Info("Deleting persistent node storage of C9s lab",
2268: +		"name", req.Name,
2269: +		"namespace", namespace,
2270: +		"claims", len(list.Items),
2271: +	)
2272: +
2273: +	for idx := range list.Items {
2274: +		err := claims.Delete(ctx, list.Items[idx].Name, metav1.DeleteOptions{})
2275: +		if err != nil && !apierrors.IsNotFound(err) {
2276: +			return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to delete persistent claim %s/%s: %w",
2277: +				namespace, list.Items[idx].Name, err)
2278: +		}
2279: +	}
2280: +
2281: +	if !req.Wait {
2282: +		return 0, nil
2283: +	}
2284: +
2285: +	// A claim is only removed once no pod uses it any more. A redeploy right after the
2286: +	// destroy must not adopt a claim that is still terminating.
2287: +	waitCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, r.timeoutFor(req.Timeout))
2288: +	defer cancel()
2289: +
2290: +	err = wait.PollUntilContextCancel(waitCtx, pollInterval, true,
2291: +		func(ctx context.Context) (bool, error) {
2292: +			remaining, err := claims.List(ctx, metav1.ListOptions{LabelSelector: selector})
2293: +			if err != nil {
2294: +				return false, fmt.Errorf("failed to list persistent claims of c9s lab %s/%s: %w",
2295: +					namespace, req.Name, err)
2296: +			}
2297: +
2298: +			return len(remaining.Items) == 0, nil
2299: +		})
2300: +	if err != nil {
2301: +		return 0, fmt.Errorf("waiting for the persistent claims of c9s lab %s/%s to be deleted: %w",
2302: +			namespace, req.Name, err)
2303: +	}
2304: +
2305: +	return 0, nil
2306: +}

2481: +func TestNewDoesNotLoadKubeconfig(t *testing.T) {
2482: +	t.Setenv(envKubeconfig, "/nonexistent/kubeconfig")
2483: +	t.Setenv("KUBECONFIG", "/nonexistent/kubeconfig")
2484: +
2485: +	lr, err := New(clablabruntime.Config{})
2486: +	if err != nil {
2487: +		t.Fatalf("New() error = %v, want the kubeconfig to be loaded lazily", err)
2488: +	}
2489: +
2490: +	req := clablabruntime.DeployRequest{
2491: +		Name:               "lab1",
2492: +		TopologyDefinition: []byte(offlineDefinition),
2493: +	}
2494: +	if err := lr.(clablabruntime.TopologyValidator).Validate(
2495: +		context.Background(),
2496: +		req,
2497: +	); err != nil {
2498: +		t.Fatalf("Validate() error = %v, want offline validation", err)
2499: +	}
2500: +	manifests, err := lr.(clablabruntime.ManifestEmitter).Manifests(context.Background(), req)
2501: +	if err != nil || len(manifests) == 0 {
2502: +		t.Fatalf("Manifests() = %d manifests, %v; want offline manifests", len(manifests), err)
2503: +	}
2504: +
2505: +	_, err = lr.Inspect(context.Background(), clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: "lab1"})
2506: +	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "Kubernetes client config") {
2507: +		t.Fatalf("Inspect() error = %v, want the kubeconfig load error", err)
2508: +	}
2509: +}

2511: +func TestConnectLoadsClientsOnce(t *testing.T) {
2512: +	t.Parallel()
2513: +
2514: +	var loads atomic.Int32
2515: +	r := &Runtime{clients: &clientLoader{
2516: +		loadConfig: func() (*rest.Config, string, error) {
2517: +			loads.Add(1)
2518: +			return &rest.Config{Host: "https://cluster.example"}, "", nil
2519: +		},
2520: +		newClients: func(cfg *rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error) {
2521: +			return &kubeClients{kube: kubefake.NewSimpleClientset(), restConfig: cfg}, nil
2522: +		},
2523: +	}}
2524: +
2525: +	for range 3 {
2526: +		view, err := r.connect()
2527: +		if err != nil {
2528: +			t.Fatal(err)
2529: +		}
2530: +		if view.kubeClient == nil || view.restConfig == nil {
2531: +			t.Fatal("connected view has no clients")
2532: +		}
2533: +		if view.namespace != defaultNamespace {
2534: +			t.Fatalf("namespace = %q, want %q", view.namespace, defaultNamespace)
2535: +		}
2536: +		again, err := view.connect()
2537: +		if err != nil || again != view {
2538: +			t.Fatalf("connect() on a connected view = %p, %v; want the view itself", again, err)
2539: +		}
2540: +	}
2541: +	if loads.Load() != 1 {
2542: +		t.Fatalf("kubeconfig loaded %d times, want 1", loads.Load())
2543: +	}
2544: +	if r.kubeClient != nil {
2545: +		t.Fatal("connect() changed the shared runtime instead of returning a view")
2546: +	}
2547: +
2548: +	failing := &Runtime{clients: &clientLoader{
2549: +		loadConfig: func() (*rest.Config, string, error) {
2550: +			return nil, "", errors.New("no kubeconfig")
2551: +		},
2552: +		newClients: newKubeClients,
2553: +	}}
2554: +	if _, err := failing.connect(); err == nil {
2555: +		t.Fatal("connect() error = nil, want the load error")
2556: +	}
2557: +}

2582: +func TestEventScopeFor(t *testing.T) {
2583: +	t.Parallel()
2584: +
2585: +	r := &Runtime{namespace: defaultNamespace}
2586: +
2587: +	tests := []struct {
2588: +		name          string
2589: +		override      string
2590: +		req           clablabruntime.EventStreamRequest
2591: +		wantNamespace string
2592: +		wantLab       string
2593: +		wantSelector  string
2594: +	}{
2595: +		{
2596: +			name:          "all namespaces",
2597: +			req:           clablabruntime.EventStreamRequest{AllNamespaces: true},
2598: +			wantNamespace: metav1.NamespaceAll,
2599: +			wantSelector:  labelTopologyOwner,
2600: +		},
2601: +		{
2602: +			name:          "namespace override",
2603: +			override:      "team-a",
2604: +			req:           clablabruntime.EventStreamRequest{AllNamespaces: true},
2605: +			wantNamespace: "team-a",
2606: +			wantSelector:  labelTopologyOwner,
2607: +		},
2608: +		{
2609: +			name:          "lab in its canonical namespace",
2610: +			req:           clablabruntime.EventStreamRequest{Name: "lab1"},
2611: +			wantNamespace: "c9s-lab1",
2612: +			wantLab:       "lab1",
2613: +			wantSelector:  labelTopologyOwner + "=lab1",
2614: +		},
2615: +		{
2616: +			name:          "lab in the override namespace",
2617: +			override:      "team-a",
2618: +			req:           clablabruntime.EventStreamRequest{Name: "lab1"},
2619: +			wantNamespace: "team-a",
2620: +			wantLab:       "lab1",
2621: +			wantSelector:  labelTopologyOwner + "=lab1",
2622: +		},
2623: +	}
2624: +
2625: +	for _, tt := range tests {
2626: +		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
2627: +			t.Parallel()
2628: +
2629: +			view := *r
2630: +			view.labNamespaceOverride = tt.override
2631: +			scope, err := view.eventScopeFor(tt.req)
2632: +			if err != nil {
2633: +				t.Fatal(err)
2634: +			}
2635: +			if scope.namespace != tt.wantNamespace || scope.lab != tt.wantLab {
2636: +				t.Fatalf("scope = %+v, want namespace %q lab %q",
2637: +					scope, tt.wantNamespace, tt.wantLab)
2638: +			}
2639: +			if got := scope.labelSelector(); got != tt.wantSelector {
2640: +				t.Fatalf("label selector = %q, want %q", got, tt.wantSelector)
2641: +			}
2642: +			fieldSelector := scope.topologyListOptions().FieldSelector
2643: +			if (tt.wantLab != "") != (fieldSelector == "metadata.name="+tt.wantLab) {
2644: +				t.Fatalf("topology field selector = %q for lab %q", fieldSelector, tt.wantLab)
2645: +			}
2646: +		})
2647: +	}
2648: +}

2816: +func TestParseInterfaceSample(t *testing.T) {
2817: +	t.Parallel()
2818: +
2819: +	output := "Inter-|   Receive |  Transmit\n" +
2820: +		" face |bytes packets errs drop fifo frame compressed multicast|bytes packets\n" +
2821: +		"    lo: 10 1 0 0 0 0 0 0 10 1 0 0 0 0 0 0\n" +
2822: +		"  eth1: 2000 20 0 0 0 0 0 0 3000 30 0 0 0 0 0 0\n" +
2823: +		interfaceSysfsMarker + "\n" +
2824: +		"eth1\t3\t9500\taa:c1:ab:00:00:01\tup\t0x1003\tto server\n" +
2825: +		"eth2\t4\t1500\taa:c1:ab:00:00:02\tlowerlayerdown\t0x1003\t\n" +
2826: +		"lo\t1\t65536\t00:00:00:00:00:00\tunknown\t0x9\t\n" +
2827: +		"dummy0\t5\t1500\t02:00:00:00:00:01\tunknown\t0x1002\t\n"
2828: +
2829: +	stats, states, hasStates, err := parseInterfaceSample([]byte(output))
2830: +	if err != nil {
2831: +		t.Fatal(err)
2832: +	}
2833: +	if !hasStates || len(stats) != 2 || len(states) != 4 {
2834: +		t.Fatalf("stats = %+v, states = %+v, hasStates = %t", stats, states, hasStates)
2835: +	}
2836: +	if stats[1].Name != "eth1" || stats[1].RxBytes != 2000 || stats[1].TxPackets != 30 {
2837: +		t.Fatalf("eth1 stats = %+v", stats[1])
2838: +	}
2839: +
2840: +	wantActions := map[string]string{"eth1": "up", "eth2": "down", "lo": "up", "dummy0": "down"}
2841: +	for _, state := range states {
2842: +		if got := state.action(); got != wantActions[state.Name] {
2843: +			t.Fatalf(
2844: +				"%s action = %q, want %q (%+v)",
2845: +				state.Name,
2846: +				got,
2847: +				wantActions[state.Name],
2848: +				state,
2849: +			)
2850: +		}
2851: +	}
2852: +	if states[0].Index != 3 || states[0].MTU != 9500 || states[0].MAC != "aa:c1:ab:00:00:01" ||
2853: +		states[0].Alias != "to server" || states[0].Flags != 0x1003 {
2854: +		t.Fatalf("eth1 state = %+v", states[0])
2855: +	}
2856: +
2857: +	stats, states, hasStates, err = parseInterfaceSample([]byte(
2858: +		"  eth1: 2000 20 0 0 0 0 0 0 3000 30 0 0 0 0 0 0\n"))
2859: +	if err != nil || hasStates || len(states) != 0 || len(stats) != 1 {
2860: +		t.Fatalf("plain /proc/net/dev = %+v %+v %t %v", stats, states, hasStates, err)
2861: +	}
2862: +}

2864: +func TestCommandNotExecutable(t *testing.T) {
2865: +	t.Parallel()
2866: +

2868: +		t.Fatal("exit codes 126/127 must mean the command cannot run")
2869: +	}
2870: +	if !commandNotExecutable(0, errors.New(`exec: "sh": executable file not found in $PATH`)) {
2871: +		t.Fatal("a missing executable must mean the command cannot run")
2872: +	}
2873: +	if commandNotExecutable(1, errors.New("connection refused")) {
2874: +		t.Fatal("other failures are not a missing command")
2875: +	}

2878: +func TestInterfacePollerEmitsStateChanges(t *testing.T) {
2879: +	t.Parallel()
2880: +
2881: +	newSample := func(ts time.Time, ifaces ...c9sIfaceState) interfaceSample {
2882: +		return interfaceSample{

2885: +				node:  clablabruntime.NodeState{Name: "r1", Pod: "lab1-r1-abc"},
2886: +				pod:   &corev1.Pod{ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Name: "lab1-r1-abc"}},
2887: +			},
2888: +			stats: []c9sIfaceStats{

2890: +			},
2891: +			ifaces:    ifaces,
2892: +			hasStates: true,
2893: +			timestamp: ts,
2894: +		}
2895: +	}
2896: +	up := c9sIfaceState{Name: "eth1", Index: 3, MTU: 9500, OperState: "up", Flags: 0x1003}
2897: +	down := c9sIfaceState{Name: "eth1", Index: 3, MTU: 9500, OperState: "down", Flags: 0x1002}
2898: +	eth2 := c9sIfaceState{Name: "eth2", Index: 4, OperState: "up", Flags: 0x1003}
2899: +
2900: +	for _, initialState := range []bool{false, true} {
2901: +		sink := make(chan clablabruntime.Event, 32)
2902: +		p := &interfacePoller{
2903: +			r:            &Runtime{},
2904: +			opts:         interfacePollOptions{includeInitialState: initialState},
2905: +			sink:         sink,
2906: +			statsSamples: map[string]c9sIfaceStatsSample{},
2907: +			nodes:        map[string]*trackedNode{},
2908: +			noShell:      map[string]bool{},
2909: +			firstRound:   true,
2910: +		}
2911: +		ctx := context.Background()
2912: +		start := time.Now()
2913: +
2914: +		p.processSample(ctx, newSample(start, up))
2915: +		if got := drain(sink); initialState != (len(got) == 1) {
2916: +			t.Fatalf("initial-state=%t: first round emitted %+v", initialState, got)
2917: +		}
2918: +
2919: +		p.firstRound = false
2920: +		p.processSample(ctx, newSample(start.Add(time.Second), up))
2921: +		if got := drain(sink); len(got) != 0 {
2922: +			t.Fatalf("unchanged interface emitted %+v", got)
2923: +		}
2924: +
2925: +		p.processSample(ctx, newSample(start.Add(2*time.Second), down, eth2))
2926: +		got := drain(sink)
2927: +		if len(got) != 2 {
2928: +			t.Fatalf("change emitted %+v, want eth1 down and new eth2 up", got)
2929: +		}
2930: +		byIf := map[string]clablabruntime.Event{}
2931: +		for _, ev := range got {
2932: +			byIf[ev.Attributes["ifname"]] = ev
2933: +		}
2934: +		ev := byIf["eth1"]
2935: +		if ev.Type != "interface" || ev.Action != "down" || ev.ActorID != "c9s-lab1/lab1/r1" ||
2936: +			ev.ActorName != "lab1-r1" || ev.ActorFullID != "lab1-r1-abc" ||
2937: +			ev.Attributes["state"] != "down" || ev.Attributes["index"] != "3" ||
2938: +			ev.Attributes["mtu"] != "9500" || ev.Attributes["origin"] != "clabernetes" ||
2939: +			ev.Attributes["lab"] != "lab1" || ev.Attributes["node"] != "r1" ||
2940: +			ev.Attributes["namespace"] != "c9s-lab1" || ev.Attributes["pod"] != "lab1-r1-abc" {
2941: +			t.Fatalf("eth1 event = %+v", ev)
2942: +		}
2943: +		if byIf["eth2"].Action != "up" {
2944: +			t.Fatalf("eth2 event = %+v", byIf["eth2"])
2945: +		}
2946: +
2947: +		// eth2 disappears
2948: +		p.processSample(ctx, newSample(start.Add(3*time.Second), down))
2949: +		got = drain(sink)
2950: +		if len(got) != 1 || got[0].Action != "down" ||
2951: +			got[0].Attributes["state"] != interfaceStateNotPresent {
2952: +			t.Fatalf("removed interface emitted %+v", got)
2953: +		}
2954: +
2955: +		// the node stops running
2956: +		p.retireStoppedNodes(ctx, map[string]bool{})
2957: +		got = drain(sink)
2958: +		if len(got) != 1 || got[0].Attributes["ifname"] != "eth1" ||
2959: +			got[0].Attributes["state"] != interfaceStateNotPresent || len(p.nodes) != 0 {
2960: +			t.Fatalf("stopped node emitted %+v, tracked %+v", got, p.nodes)
2961: +		}
2962: +	}
2963: +}

3217: +func newestPod(current, candidate *corev1.Pod) *corev1.Pod {
3218: +	if current == nil {
3219: +		return candidate
3220: +	}
3221: +
3222: +	currentRunning := current.Status.Phase == corev1.PodRunning
3223: +	candidateRunning := candidate.Status.Phase == corev1.PodRunning

3225: +		if candidateRunning {

3230: +	}
3231: +

3233: +		return candidate
3234: +	}
3235: +
3236: +	return current
3237: +}

113: func graphFn(ctx context.Context, o *Options) error {
114: 	c, err := clabcore.NewContainerLab(o.ToClabOptions()...)
115: 	if err != nil {
116: 		return err
117: 	}
118: 
119: 	// Lab runtimes do not build the topology's nodes; the graph modes they support render
120: 	// from the topology file, so the nodes are built here without a container runtime.
121: 	if err := c.LoadTopologyNodes(); err != nil {
122: 		return err
123: 	}
124: 
125: 	err = c.ResolveLinks()
126: 	if err != nil {
127: 		return err
128: 	}
129: 
130: 	if o.Graph.GenerateDotFile {
131: 		return c.GenerateDotGraph(ctx)
132: 	}
133: 
134: 	if o.Graph.GenerateMermaid {
135: 		return c.GenerateMermaidGraph(o.Graph.MermaidDirection)
136: 	}
137: 
138: 	if o.Graph.GenerateDrawIO {
139: 		return c.GenerateDrawioDiagram(o.Graph.DrawIOVersion, o.Graph.DrawIOArgs)
140: 	}
141: 
142: 	gtopo := clabcore.GraphTopo{
143: 		Nodes: make([]clabtypes.ContainerDetails, 0, len(c.Nodes)),
144: 		Links: make([]clabcore.Link, 0, len(c.Links)),
145: 	}
146: 
147: 	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
148: 	defer cancel()
149: 
150: 	var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
151: 	// if offline mode is not enforced, list containers matching lab name
152: 	if !o.Graph.Offline {
153: 		containers, err = c.ListContainers(ctx,
154: 			clabcore.WithListLabName(c.Config.Name))
155: 		if err != nil {
156: 			return err
157: 		}
158: 
159: 		log.Debugf("found %d containers", len(containers))
160: 	}
161: 
162: 	switch {
163: 	case len(containers) == 0:
164: 		c.BuildGraphFromTopo(&gtopo)
165: 	case len(containers) > 0:
166: 		c.BuildGraphFromDeployedLab(&gtopo, containers)
167: 	}
168: 
169: 	sort.Slice(gtopo.Nodes, func(i, j int) bool {
170: 		return gtopo.Nodes[i].Name < gtopo.Nodes[j].Name
171: 	})
172: 
173: 	for _, l := range c.Links {
174: 		eps := l.GetEndpoints()
175: 		// Skip links that are not point-to-point (e.g. dummy, host, macvlan,
176: 		// mgmt-net links expose a single endpoint). Indexing eps[1] on such
177: 		// links would panic, so they are not rendered as edges.
178: 		if len(eps) != 2 {
179: 			log.Debugf(
180: 				"skipping non point-to-point link with %d endpoint(s) in graph topology",
181: 				len(eps),
182: 			)
183: 			continue

79: // NewContainerLab function defines a new container lab.
80: func NewContainerLab(opts ...ClabOption) (*CLab, error) {
81: 	c := &CLab{
82: 		Config: &Config{
83: 			Mgmt:     new(clabtypes.MgmtNet),
84: 			Topology: clabtypes.NewTopology(),
85: 		},
86: 		TopoPaths:         &clabtypes.TopoPaths{},
87: 		m:                 new(sync.RWMutex),
88: 		Nodes:             make(map[string]clabnodes.Node),
89: 		Links:             make(map[int]clablinks.Link),
90: 		Runtimes:          make(map[string]clabruntime.ContainerRuntime),
91: 		Cert:              &clabcert.Cert{},
92: 		checkBindsPaths:   true,
93: 		dependencyManager: clabcoredependency_manager.NewDependencyManager(),
94: 	}
95: 
96: 	c.Reg = clabnodes.NewNodeRegistry()
97: 	c.RegisterNodes()
98: 
99: 	for _, opt := range opts {
100: 		err := opt(c)
101: 		if err != nil {
102: 			return nil, err
103: 		}
104: 	}
105: 
106: 	var err error
107: 	if c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileIsSet() {
108: 		if c.LabRuntime != nil {
109: 			err = c.prepareLabRuntimeTopology()
110: 		} else {
111: 			err = c.parseTopology()
112: 		}
113: 	}
114: 
115: 	// Extract the host systems DNS servers and populate the
116: 	// Nodes DNS Config with these if not specifically provided
117: 	fileSystem := os.DirFS("/")
118: 	if err := c.extractDNSServers(fileSystem); err != nil {
119: 		return nil, err
120: 	}
121: 
122: 	return c, err
123: }

125: // RuntimeInitializer returns a runtime initializer function for a provided runtime name.
126: // Order of preference: cli flag -> env var -> default value of docker.
127: func RuntimeInitializer(name string) (string, clabruntime.Initializer, error) {
128: 	name = resolveRuntimeName(name)
129: 
130: 	runtimeInitializer, ok := clabruntime.ContainerRuntimes[name]
131: 	if !ok {

64: // ParseTopology parses the lab topology.
65: func (c *CLab) parseTopology() error {
66: 	log.Info("Parsing & checking topology", "file", c.TopoPaths.TopologyFilenameBase())
67: 
68: 	if strings.Contains(c.Config.Name, gitBranchVar) ||
69: 		strings.Contains(c.Config.Name, gitHashVar) {
70: 		r := c.magicTopoNameReplacer()
71: 		oldName := c.Config.Name
72: 		c.Config.Name = r.Replace(c.Config.Name)
73: 		log.Debugf(
74: 			"Topology name contains Git variables, substituted topology name: %q -> %q",
75: 			oldName,
76: 			c.Config.Name,
77: 		)
78: 	}
79: 
80: 	err := c.TopoPaths.SetLabDirByPrefix(c.Config.Name)
81: 	if err != nil {
82: 		return err
83: 	}
84: 
85: 	if c.Config.Prefix == nil {
86: 		c.Config.Prefix = new(string)
87: 		*c.Config.Prefix = defaultPrefix
88: 	}
89: 
90: 	if err := c.validateKindSpecificConfigKeys(); err != nil {
91: 		return err
92: 	}
93: 
94: 	// initialize Nodes and Links variable
95: 	c.Nodes = make(map[string]clabnodes.Node)
96: 	c.Links = make(map[int]clablinks.Link)
97: 
98: 	// initialize the Node information from the topology map
99: 	nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Config.Topology.Nodes))
100: 	for nodeName := range c.Config.Topology.Nodes {
101: 		nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
102: 	}
103: 
104: 	sort.Strings(nodeNames)
105: 
106: 	// collect node runtimes in a map[NodeName] -> RuntimeName
107: 	nodeRuntimes := make(map[string]string)
108: 
109: 	for nodeName, topologyNode := range c.Config.Topology.Nodes {
110: 		// this case is when runtime was overridden at the node level
111: 		if r := c.Config.Topology.GetNodeRuntime(nodeName); r != "" {
112: 			nodeRuntimes[nodeName] = r
113: 			continue
114: 		}
115: 
116: 		// this case if for non-default runtimes overriding the global default
117: 		if topologyNode != nil {
118: 			if r, ok := clabnodes.NonDefaultRuntimes[topologyNode.Kind]; ok {
119: 				nodeRuntimes[nodeName] = r
120: 				continue
121: 			}
122: 		}
123: 
124: 		// saving the global default runtime
125: 		nodeRuntimes[nodeName] = c.globalRuntimeName
126: 	}
127: 
128: 	// initialize any extra runtimes
129: 	for _, r := range nodeRuntimes {
130: 		// Nodes of a lab runtime are only described here; they are not run by a local
131: 		// container runtime.
132: 		if c.LabRuntime != nil {
133: 			break

135:

138: 			continue
139: 		}
140:

142: 			newRuntime := rInit()
143: 			defaultConfig := c.Runtimes[c.globalRuntimeName].Config()
144: 
145: 			err := newRuntime.Init(
146: 				clabruntime.WithConfig(&defaultConfig),
147: 			)
148: 			if err != nil {
149: 				return fmt.Errorf("failed to init the container runtime: %s", err)

151: 
152: 			c.Runtimes[r] = newRuntime
153: 		}

158: 		if err != nil {
159: 			return err
160: 		}
161: 	}
162: 
163: 	return c.injectTailscaleSidecars()
164: }

37: 		// --reconfigure regenerates the lab from scratch, like removing a local lab
38: 		// directory, so it also deletes the persistent node storage.
39: 		err := c.LabRuntime.Destroy(ctx, clablabruntime.DestroyRequest{
40: 			Name:       c.Config.Name,
41: 			Wait:       true,
42: 			Timeout:    c.timeout,
43: 			MaxWorkers: options.maxWorkers,
44: 			Cleanup:    true,
45: 		})
46: 		if err != nil {
47: 			return nil, err
48: 		}
49: 	}
50: 
51: 	req, err := c.labRuntimeDeployRequest()
52: 	if err != nil {
53: 		return nil, err
54: 	}
55: 	req.Wait = true
56: 	applyLabRuntimeDeployOptions(&req, options)
57: 
58: 	state, err := c.LabRuntime.Deploy(ctx, req)
59: 	if err != nil {
60: 		return nil, err
61: 	}
62: 
63: 	return c.containersFromLabState(state), nil
64: }
65: 
66: func (c *CLab) labRuntimeDeployRequest() (clablabruntime.DeployRequest, error) {
67: 	if c.Config.Name == "" {
68: 		return clablabruntime.DeployRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")
69: 	}
70: 	if len(c.renderedTopology) == 0 {
71: 		return clablabruntime.DeployRequest{}, fmt.Errorf("rendered topology is empty")
72: 	}
73: 
74: 	topologyFile := ""
75: 	topologyLabDir := ""
76: 	if c.TopoPaths != nil {
77: 		topologyFile = c.TopoPaths.TopologyFilenameAbsPath()
78: 		topologyLabDir = c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir()
79: 	}
80: 
81: 	return clablabruntime.DeployRequest{
82: 		Name:               c.Config.Name,
83: 		Owner:              c.labOwner(),
84: 		TopologyFile:       topologyFile,
85: 		TopologyLabDir:     topologyLabDir,
86: 		TopologyDefinition: c.renderedTopology,
87: 		Timeout:            c.timeout,
88: 	}, nil
89: }
90: 
91: // applyLabRuntimeDeployOptions copies the deploy options that shape remote resources onto the
92: // runtime request in one place, so every path that builds a request agrees on them.
93: func applyLabRuntimeDeployOptions(req *clablabruntime.DeployRequest, options *DeployOptions) {
94: 	if options == nil {
95: 		return
96: 	}
97: 
98: 	req.NoTopologyCR = options.noTopologyCR
99: 	req.ImagePullSecret = options.imagePullSecret
100: 	req.ExposeType = options.exposeType
101: 	req.NoPersistence = options.noPersistence
102: 	req.MaxWorkers = options.maxWorkers
103: }
104: 
105: // LabRuntimeManifests renders the remote resources the selected runtime would create for the
106: // topology, shaped by the same deploy options a real deployment honors, without contacting the
107: // runtime's backend.
108: func (c *CLab) LabRuntimeManifests(
109: 	ctx context.Context,
110: 	options *DeployOptions,
111: ) ([]clablabruntime.Manifest, error) {
112: 	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
113: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no lab runtime selected")
114: 	}
115: 
116: 	emitter, ok := c.LabRuntime.(clablabruntime.ManifestEmitter)
117: 	if !ok {
118: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf(
119: 			"lab runtime %q does not support emitting manifests",
120: 			c.globalRuntimeName,
121: 		)
122: 	}
123: 
124: 	req, err := c.labRuntimeDeployRequest()
125: 	if err != nil {
126: 		return nil, err
127: 	}
128: 	applyLabRuntimeDeployOptions(&req, options)
129: 
130: 	return emitter.Manifests(ctx, req)
131: }
132: 
133: // ValidateLabRuntimeTopology executes the selected runtime's compiler without mutation.
134: func (c *CLab) ValidateLabRuntimeTopology(ctx context.Context) error {
135: 	if c.LabRuntime == nil {
136: 		return fmt.Errorf("no lab runtime selected")
137: 	}
138: 
139: 	validator, ok := c.LabRuntime.(clablabruntime.TopologyValidator)
140: 	if !ok {
141: 		return fmt.Errorf(
142: 			"lab runtime %q does not support topology validation",
143: 			c.globalRuntimeName,
144: 		)
145: 	}
146: 
147: 	req, err := c.labRuntimeDeployRequest()
148: 	if err != nil {
149: 		return err
150: 	}
151: 
152: 	return validator.Validate(ctx, req)
153: }
154: 
155: func (c *CLab) destroyWithLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, opts *DestroyOptions) error {
156: 	if len(opts.nodeFilter) != 0 {
157: 		return fmt.Errorf(
158: 			"node-filter is not supported for lab runtime %q; no resources were deleted",
159: 			c.globalRuntimeName,
160: 		)
161: 	}
162: 
163: 	if opts.all {
164: 		return c.destroyAllWithLabRuntime(ctx, opts)
165: 	}
166: 
167: 	if c.Config.Name == "" {
168: 		return fmt.Errorf("topology name is required")
169: 	}
170: 
171: 	err := c.LabRuntime.Destroy(ctx, clablabruntime.DestroyRequest{
172: 		Name:       c.Config.Name,
173: 		Wait:       true,
174: 		Timeout:    c.timeout,
175: 		MaxWorkers: opts.maxWorkers,
176: 		Cleanup:    opts.cleanup,
177: 	})
178: 	if err != nil {
179: 		return err
180: 	}
181: 
182: 	if opts.cleanup {
183: 		return c.cleanupLabRuntimeLabDir()
184: 	}
185: 
186: 	return nil
187: }
188: 
189: // cleanupLabRuntimeLabDir removes the local lab directory for --cleanup parity with local
190: // runtimes. Controller-driven runtimes keep node state remotely, so the directory usually only
191: // exists when a lab was previously deployed locally or configs were copied out.
192: func (c *CLab) cleanupLabRuntimeLabDir() error {
193: 	if c.TopoPaths == nil || !c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileIsSet() {
194: 		return nil
195: 	}
196: 
197: 	labDir := c.TopoPaths.TopologyLabDir()
198: 	if labDir == "" {
199: 		return nil
200: 	}
201: 	if _, err := os.Stat(labDir); os.IsNotExist(err) {
202: 		return nil
203: 	}
204: 
205: 	log.Info("Removing lab directory", "path", labDir)
206: 
207: 	if err := os.RemoveAll(labDir); err != nil {
208: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to remove lab directory %q: %w", labDir, err)
209: 	}
210: 
211: 	return nil
212: }
213: 
214: func (c *CLab) destroyAllWithLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, opts *DestroyOptions) error {
215: 	states, err := c.LabRuntime.List(ctx, clablabruntime.ListRequest{AllNamespaces: true})
216: 	if err != nil {
217: 		return err
218: 	}
219: 
220: 	if len(states) == 0 {
221: 		log.Info("no clabernetes topologies found")
222: 		return nil
223: 	}
224: 
225: 	topos := make(map[string]string, len(states))
226: 	for _, state := range states {
227: 		topos[state.TopologyPath] = ""
228: 	}
229: 
230: 	if opts.terminalPrompt && term.IsTerminal(int(os.Stdin.Fd())) {
231: 		if err := cliPromptToDestroyAll(topos); err != nil {
232: 			return err
233: 		}
234: 	}
235: 
236: 	var errs []error
237: 	for _, state := range states {
238: 		if err := c.LabRuntime.Destroy(ctx, clablabruntime.DestroyRequest{
239: 			Name:       state.Name,
240: 			Namespace:  state.Namespace,
241: 			Wait:       true,
242: 			Timeout:    c.timeout,
243: 			MaxWorkers: opts.maxWorkers,
244: 			Cleanup:    opts.cleanup,
245: 		}); err != nil {
246: 			errs = append(errs, err)
247: 		}
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	if len(errs) != 0 {
251: 		return fmt.Errorf("error(s) occurred during clabernetes topology deletion: %w",
252: 			errors.Join(errs...))
253: 	}
254: 
255: 	return nil
256: }
257: 
258: func (c *CLab) ListLabRuntimeContainers(
259: 	ctx context.Context,
260: 	all bool,
261: 	options ...ListOption,
262: ) ([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, error) {
263: 	opts := NewListOptions()
264: 	for _, opt := range options {
265: 		opt(opts)
266: 	}
267: 
268: 	if all || c.Config.Name == "" {
269: 		states, err := c.LabRuntime.List(ctx, clablabruntime.ListRequest{AllNamespaces: true})
270: 		if err != nil {
271: 			return nil, err
272: 		}
273: 
274: 		var containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer
275: 		for _, state := range states {
276: 			containers = append(containers, c.containersFromLabState(state)...)
277: 		}
278: 
279: 		return filterLabRuntimeContainers(containers, opts.ToFilters()), nil
280: 	}
281: 
282: 	state, err := c.LabRuntime.Inspect(ctx, clablabruntime.InspectRequest{Name: c.Config.Name})
283: 	if err != nil {
284: 		return nil, err
285: 	}
286: 
287: 	return filterLabRuntimeContainers(c.containersFromLabState(state), opts.ToFilters()), nil
288: }
289: 
290: func (c *CLab) execWithLabRuntime(
291: 	ctx context.Context,
292: 	cmds []string,
293: 	listOptions ...ListOption,
294: ) (*clabexec.ExecCollection, error) {
295: 	containers, err := c.ListLabRuntimeContainers(ctx, false, listOptions...)
296: 	if err != nil {
297: 		return nil, err
298: 	}
299: 	if len(containers) == 0 {
300: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("filter did not match any containers")
301: 	}
302: 
303: 	var execCmds []*clabexec.ExecCmd
304: 	for _, execCmdStr := range cmds {
305: 		execCmd, err := clabexec.NewExecCmdFromString(execCmdStr)
306: 		if err != nil {
307: 			return nil, err
308: 		}
309: 		execCmds = append(execCmds, execCmd)
310: 	}
311: 
312: 	resultCollection := clabexec.NewExecCollection()
313: 	var execErrors []error
314: 	for idx := range containers {
315: 		namespace, labName, nodeName, err := labRuntimeContainerParts(containers[idx])
316: 		if err != nil {
317: 			log.Warnf("exec target %s is invalid: %v", containers[idx].Names[0], err)
318: 			execErrors = append(execErrors, fmt.Errorf(
319: 				"exec target %s is invalid: %w", containers[idx].Names[0], err))
320: 			continue
321: 		}
322: 
323: 		for _, execCmd := range execCmds {
324: 			result, err := c.LabRuntime.Exec(ctx, clablabruntime.ExecRequest{
325: 				Name:      labName,
326: 				Namespace: namespace,
327: 				NodeName:  nodeName,
328: 				Command:   execCmd.GetCmd(),
329: 			})
330: 			if err != nil {
331: 				log.Warnf("exec on %s failed: %v", containers[idx].Names[0], err)
332: 				execErrors = append(execErrors, fmt.Errorf(
333: 					"exec on %s failed: %w", containers[idx].Names[0], err))
334: 				continue
335: 			}
336: 
337: 			resultCollection.Add(containers[idx].Names[0], result)
338: 			if result.GetReturnCode() != 0 {
339: 				execErrors = append(execErrors, fmt.Errorf(
340: 					"exec on %s returned exit code %d",
341: 					containers[idx].Names[0],
342: 					result.GetReturnCode(),
343: 				))
344: 			}
345: 		}
346: 	}
347: 
348: 	return resultCollection, errors.Join(execErrors...)
349: }
350: 
351: func (c *CLab) startNodesWithLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, nodeNames []string) error {
352: 	return c.LabRuntime.Start(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
353: 		Name:    c.Config.Name,
354: 		Nodes:   nodeNames,
355: 		Timeout: c.timeout,
356: 	})
357: }

360: 	return c.LabRuntime.Stop(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
361: 		Name:    c.Config.Name,
362: 		Nodes:   nodeNames,
363: 		Timeout: c.timeout,
364: 	})
365: }

367: func (c *CLab) restartNodesWithLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, nodeNames []string) error {
368: 	return c.LabRuntime.Restart(ctx, clablabruntime.NodeRequest{
369: 		Name:    c.Config.Name,
370: 		Nodes:   nodeNames,
371: 		Timeout: c.timeout,

373: }

375: func (c *CLab) saveWithLabRuntime(ctx context.Context, opts *SaveOptions) error {
376: 	if opts.copyDst != "" {
377: 		resolvedDst, err := c.resolveCopyOutDst(opts.copyDst)
378: 		if err != nil {
379: 			return err
380: 		}
381: 		opts.copyDst = resolvedDst
382: 	}
383: 
384: 	result, err := c.LabRuntime.Save(ctx, clablabruntime.SaveRequest{
385: 		Name:  c.Config.Name,
386: 		Nodes: c.nodeFilter,
387: 		Copy:  opts.copyDst != "",
388: 	})
389: 	if err != nil {
390: 		return err
391: 	}
392: 
393: 	if opts.copyDst == "" || result == nil {
394: 		return nil
395: 	}
396: 
397: 	return c.copyLabRuntimeSavedFiles(result, opts.copyDst)
398: }
399: 
400: func (c *CLab) containersFromLabState(
401: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
402: ) []clabruntime.GenericContainer {
403: 	if state == nil {
404: 		return nil
405: 	}
406: 
407: 	nodes := state.Nodes
408: 	if len(nodes) == 0 && c.Config.Topology != nil {
409: 		nodeNames := make([]string, 0, len(c.Config.Topology.Nodes))
410: 		for nodeName := range c.Config.Topology.Nodes {
411: 			nodeNames = append(nodeNames, nodeName)
412: 		}
413: 		sort.Strings(nodeNames)
414: 
415: 		nodes = make([]clablabruntime.NodeState, 0, len(nodeNames))
416: 		for _, nodeName := range nodeNames {
417: 			nodes = append(nodes, clablabruntime.NodeState{
418: 				Name:  nodeName,
419: 				Kind:  c.Config.Topology.GetNodeKind(nodeName),
420: 				Image: c.Config.Topology.GetNodeImage(nodeName),
421: 				State: state.State,
422: 				Ready: state.Ready,
423: 			})
424: 		}
425: 	}
426: 
427: 	containers := make([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, 0, len(nodes))
428: 	for _, node := range nodes {
429: 		containers = append(containers, c.containerFromLabNode(state, node))
430: 	}
431: 
432: 	return containers
433: }
434: 
435: func (c *CLab) containerFromLabNode(
436: 	state *clablabruntime.LabState,
437: 	node clablabruntime.NodeState,
438: ) clabruntime.GenericContainer {
439: 	nodeName := fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s", state.Name, node.Name)
440: 	containerState := node.State
441: 	containerStatus := node.State
442: 	if containerState == "" {
443: 		containerState = state.State
444: 	}
445: 	if node.Ready {
446: 		containerState = "running"
447: 		containerStatus = "healthy"
448: 	}
449: 
450: 	labels := map[string]string{
451: 		clabconstants.Containerlab: state.Name,
452: 		clabconstants.NodeName:     node.Name,
453: 		clabconstants.LongName:     nodeName,
454: 		clabconstants.TopoFile:     labRuntimeTopologyPath(c, state),
455: 	}
456: 
457: 	var image string
458: 	if c.Config.Topology != nil {
459: 		topologyNode := c.topologyNodeName(node.Name)
460: 		labels[clabconstants.NodeKind] = c.Config.Topology.GetNodeKind(topologyNode)
461: 		image = c.Config.Topology.GetNodeImage(topologyNode)
462: 
463: 		if group := c.Config.Topology.GetNodeGroup(topologyNode); group != "" {
464: 			labels[clabconstants.NodeGroup] = group
465: 		}
466: 	}
467: 	if node.Kind != "" {
468: 		labels[clabconstants.NodeKind] = node.Kind
469: 	}
470: 	if node.Image != "" {
471: 		image = node.Image
472: 	}
473: 
474: 	if state.Owner != "" {
475: 		labels[clabconstants.Owner] = state.Owner
476: 	} else if c.customOwner != "" {
477: 		labels[clabconstants.Owner] = c.customOwner
478: 	}
479: 
480: 	// The ID names the node uniquely across namespaces and labs. It is also the short ID, so
481: 	// inspect reports it as container_id and it matches the events actor ID.
482: 	id := labRuntimeContainerID(state.Namespace, state.Name, node.Name)
483: 
484: 	return clabruntime.GenericContainer{
485: 		Names:           []string{nodeName},
486: 		ID:              id,
487: 		ShortID:         id,
488: 		Image:           image,
489: 		State:           containerState,
490: 		Status:          containerStatus,
491: 		Labels:          labels,
492: 		NetworkName:     state.Namespace,
493: 		NetworkSettings: managementAddress(node),
494: 		Workload: &clabtypes.LabRuntimeWorkload{
495: 			Namespace:           state.Namespace,
496: 			Pod:                 node.Pod,
497: 			Container:           node.Container,
498: 			NodeUID:             node.NodeUID,
499: 			ExposedPorts:        node.ExposedPorts,
500: 			LoadBalancerAddress: node.LoadBalancerAddress,
501: 		},
502: 	}
503: }
504: 
505: // labRuntimeContainerID is the ID of a lab runtime node: <namespace>/<lab>/<node>.
506: func labRuntimeContainerID(namespace, lab, node string) string {
507: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%s/%s/%s", namespace, lab, node)
508: }
509: 
510: // topologyNodeName maps a node name a lab runtime reports back onto the topology node it belongs
511: // to. The runtime renames the nodes Kubernetes cannot carry, so the state it reports does not
512: // always use the name the topology file wrote.
513: func (c *CLab) topologyNodeName(name string) string {
514: 	if c.Config.Topology == nil {
515: 		return name
516: 	}
517: 	if _, ok := c.Config.Topology.Nodes[name]; ok {
518: 		return name
519: 	}
520: 
521: 	for nodeName := range c.Config.Topology.Nodes {
522: 		if clabnames.SanitizeName(nodeName) == name {
523: 			return nodeName
524: 		}
525: 	}
526: 
527: 	return name
528: }
529: 
530: // managementAddress reports the address a user reaches the node at: the LoadBalancer address
531: // when the node is exposed, otherwise the allocated management address.
532: func managementAddress(node clablabruntime.NodeState) clabruntime.GenericMgmtIPs {
533: 	settings := clabruntime.GenericMgmtIPs{}
534: 
535: 	if ip := net.ParseIP(node.LoadBalancerAddress); ip != nil {
536: 		if ip.To4() != nil {
537: 			settings.IPv4addr = node.LoadBalancerAddress
538: 			settings.IPv4pLen = 32
539: 		} else {
540: 			settings.IPv6addr = node.LoadBalancerAddress
541: 			settings.IPv6pLen = 128
542: 		}
543: 	}
544: 
545: 	if settings.IPv4addr == "" {
546: 		settings.IPv4addr, settings.IPv4pLen = splitManagementCIDR(node.MgmtIPv4Address)
547: 	}
548: 	if settings.IPv6addr == "" {
549: 		settings.IPv6addr, settings.IPv6pLen = splitManagementCIDR(node.MgmtIPv6Address)
550: 	}
551: 
552: 	return settings
553: }
554: 
555: func splitManagementCIDR(cidr string) (string, int) {
556: 	if cidr == "" {
557: 		return "", 0
558: 	}
559: 
560: 	ip, network, err := net.ParseCIDR(cidr)
561: 	if err != nil {
562: 		if net.ParseIP(cidr) != nil {
563: 			return cidr, 0
564: 		}
565: 
566: 		return "", 0
567: 	}
568: 
569: 	prefixLen, _ := network.Mask.Size()
570: 
571: 	return ip.String(), prefixLen
572: }
573: 
574: func labRuntimeTopologyPath(c *CLab, state *clablabruntime.LabState) string {
575: 	if c.TopoPaths.TopologyFileIsSet() {
576: 		return c.TopoPaths.TopologyFilenameAbsPath()
577: 	}
578: 
579: 	if state.TopologyPath != "" {
580: 		return state.TopologyPath
581: 	}
582: 
583: 	return fmt.Sprintf("k8s://%s/topologies/%s", state.Namespace, state.Name)
584: }
585: 
586: func labRuntimeContainerParts(c clabruntime.GenericContainer) (string, string, string, error) {
587: 	parts := strings.Split(c.ID, "/")
588: 	if len(parts) != 3 {
589: 		return "", "", "", fmt.Errorf("expected namespace/lab/node id, got %q", c.ID)
590: 	}
591: 
592: 	return parts[0], parts[1], parts[2], nil
593: }
594: 
595: func filterLabRuntimeContainers(
596: 	containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,
597: 	filters []*clabtypes.GenericFilter,
598: ) []clabruntime.GenericContainer {
599: 	if len(filters) == 0 {
600: 		return containers
601: 	}
602: 
603: 	filtered := make([]clabruntime.GenericContainer, 0, len(containers))
604: 	for _, container := range containers {
605: 		if labRuntimeContainerMatches(container, filters) {
606: 			filtered = append(filtered, container)
607: 		}
608: 	}
609: 
610: 	return filtered
611: }
612: 
613: func labRuntimeContainerMatches(
614: 	container clabruntime.GenericContainer,
615: 	filters []*clabtypes.GenericFilter,
616: ) bool {
617: 	for _, filter := range filters {
618: 		switch filter.FilterType {
619: 		case "name":
620: 			if !labRuntimeNameMatches(container.Names, filter.Match) {
621: 				return false
622: 			}
623: 		case "id":
624: 			if container.ID != filter.Match && !strings.HasPrefix(container.ID, filter.Match) {
625: 				return false
626: 			}
627: 		case "label":
628: 			if !labRuntimeLabelMatches(container.Labels, filter) {
629: 				return false
630: 			}
631: 		}
632: 	}
633: 
634: 	return true
635: }
636: 
637: func labRuntimeNameMatches(names []string, match string) bool {
638: 	for _, name := range names {
639: 		if name == match || strings.Contains(name, match) {
640: 			return true
641: 		}
642: 	}
643: 
644: 	return false
645: }
646: 
647: func labRuntimeLabelMatches(labels map[string]string, filter *clabtypes.GenericFilter) bool {
648: 	value, ok := labels[filter.Field]
649: 
650: 	switch filter.Operator {
651: 	case "exists":
652: 		return ok
653: 	case "!=":
654: 		return !ok || value != filter.Match
655: 	default:
656: 		return ok && value == filter.Match
657: 	}
658: }
659: 
660: func (c *CLab) copyLabRuntimeSavedFiles(
661: 	result *clablabruntime.SaveResult,
662: 	dstRoot string,
663: ) error {
664: 	for _, file := range result.Files {
665: 		if file.NodeName == "" || file.Name == "" {
666: 			continue
667: 		}
668: 
669: 		relPath, ok := cleanLabRuntimeSavedPath(file.Name)
670: 		if !ok {
671: 			return fmt.Errorf("refusing to copy unsafe saved config path %q", file.Name)
672: 		}
673: 
674: 		nodeDstDir := filepath.Join(dstRoot, file.NodeName)
675: 		dstPath := filepath.Join(nodeDstDir, relPath)
676: 		if err := os.MkdirAll(
677: 			filepath.Dir(dstPath),
678: 			clabconstants.PermissionsDirDefault,

200: 		}
201: 	}
202: 
203: 	for {
204: 		select {
205: 		case <-ctx.Done():
206: 			return
207: 		case err, ok := <-runtimeErrs:

210: 			}

212: 			if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {

230: 		}

399: func emitContainerSnapshots(
400: 	ctx context.Context,
401: 	containers []clabruntime.GenericContainer,
402: 	sink chan<- aggregatedEvent,
403: ) {
404: 	for idx := range containers {
405: 		container := containers[idx]

415: 		select {
416: 		case sink <- event:
417: 		case <-ctx.Done():
418: 			return
419: 		}
420: 	}

423: func aggregatedEventFromContainerSnapshot(

453:

456: 	}
457: 
458: 	if container.NetworkName != "" {
459: 		attributes["network"] = container.NetworkName
460: 	}
461: 
462: 	if container.NetworkSettings.IPv4addr != "" {
463: 		attributes["mgmt_ipv4"] = container.GetContainerIPv4()
464: 	}
465: 
466: 	if container.NetworkSettings.IPv6addr != "" {
467: 		attributes["mgmt_ipv6"] = container.GetContainerIPv6()
468: 	}
469: 
470: 	if ports := exposedPortsAttributeValue(container.Ports); ports != "" {
471: 		attributes["ports"] = ports

474: 	if len(attributes) == 0 {

478: 	actorName := firstContainerName(container)

509: func isRunningContainer(container *clabruntime.GenericContainer) bool {

517: func exposedPortsAttributeValue(ports []*clabtypes.GenericPortBinding) string {
518: 	if len(ports) == 0 {
519: 		return ""
520: 	}
521: 
522: 	sortedPorts := make([]*clabtypes.GenericPortBinding, 0, len(ports))
523: 	for idx := range ports {
524: 		if ports[idx] != nil {
525: 			sortedPorts = append(sortedPorts, ports[idx])
526: 		}
527: 	}
528: 
529: 	if len(sortedPorts) == 0 {
530: 		return ""
531: 	}
532: 
533: 	sort.Slice(sortedPorts, func(i, j int) bool {
534: 		left := sortedPorts[i]
535: 		right := sortedPorts[j]
536: 
537: 		switch {
538: 		case left.ContainerPort != right.ContainerPort:
539: 			return left.ContainerPort < right.ContainerPort
540: 		case left.Protocol != right.Protocol:
541: 			return left.Protocol < right.Protocol
542: 		case left.HostPort != right.HostPort:
543: 			return left.HostPort < right.HostPort
544: 		default:
545: 			return left.HostIP < right.HostIP
546: 		}
547: 	})
548: 
549: 	result := make([]string, 0, len(sortedPorts))
550: 	for idx := range sortedPorts {
551: 		formatted := formatExposedPort(sortedPorts[idx])
552: 		if formatted != "" {
553: 			result = append(result, formatted)
554: 		}
555: 	}
556: 
557: 	if len(result) == 0 {
558: 		return ""
559: 	}
560: 
561: 	return strings.Join(result, ";")
562: }
563: 
564: func formatExposedPort(port *clabtypes.GenericPortBinding) string {
565: 	if port == nil {
566: 		return ""
567: 	}
568: 
569: 	proto := strings.TrimSpace(strings.ToLower(port.Protocol))
570: 	protoSuffix := ""
571: 	if proto != "" {
572: 		protoSuffix = "/" + proto
573: 	}
574: 
575: 	if port.HostPort > 0 {
576: 		hostIP := port.HostIP
577: 		if hostIP == "" {
578: 			hostIP = "0.0.0.0"
579: 		}
580: 
581: 		if strings.Contains(hostIP, ":") {
582: 			hostIP = fmt.Sprintf("[%s]", hostIP)
583: 		}
584: 
585: 		if port.ContainerPort > 0 {
586: 			return fmt.Sprintf(
587: 				"%s:%d%s->%d",
588: 				hostIP,
589: 				port.HostPort,
590: 				protoSuffix,
591: 				port.ContainerPort,
592: 			)
593: 		}
594: 
595: 		return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d%s", hostIP, port.HostPort, protoSuffix)
596: 	}
597: 
598: 	if port.ContainerPort <= 0 {
599: 		return ""
600: 	}
601: 
602: 	return fmt.Sprintf("%d%s", port.ContainerPort, protoSuffix)
603: }

67: type Runtime struct {
68: 	client     dynamic.Interface
69: 	kubeClient kubernetes.Interface
70: 	restConfig *rest.Config
71: 	namespace  string
72: 	// labNamespaceOverride is set by --namespace or CLAB_KUBE_NAMESPACE. When
73: 	// empty, lab-scoped operations derive their namespace from the lab name.
74: 	labNamespaceOverride string
75: 	timeout              time.Duration
76: 	// kindLinkApplyMode resolves the default link apply mode a node kind declares.
77: 	// The plan uses it to predict the pod lifecycle impact of link changes.
78: 	kindLinkApplyMode func(kind string) string
79: 	// clients loads the Kubernetes clients on first use. Commands that only compile the
80: 	// topology (validate, deploy --emit-crs) never call it, so they work without a
81: 	// kubeconfig that loads. It is nil when the clients were injected (tests).
82: 	clients *clientLoader
83: 	// connected marks a runtime view whose client fields are populated.
84: 	connected bool
85: }
86: 
87: // kubeClients is the set of Kubernetes clients a runtime view operates with.
88: type kubeClients struct {
89: 	dynamic    dynamic.Interface
90: 	kube       kubernetes.Interface
91: 	restConfig *rest.Config
92: }
93: 
94: // clientLoader loads the kubeconfig once and builds the Kubernetes clients from it.
95: type clientLoader struct {
96: 	loadConfig func() (*rest.Config, string, error)
97: 	newClients func(*rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error)
98: 
99: 	once      sync.Once
100: 	clients   *kubeClients
101: 	namespace string
102: 	err       error
103: }
104: 
105: func newClientLoader() *clientLoader {
106: 	return &clientLoader{
107: 		loadConfig: kubeClientConfig,
108: 		newClients: newKubeClients,
109: 	}
110: }
111: 
112: func newKubeClients(restConfig *rest.Config) (*kubeClients, error) {
113: 	client, err := dynamic.NewForConfig(restConfig)
114: 	if err != nil {
115: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes dynamic client: %w", err)
116: 	}
117: 
118: 	kubeClient, err := kubernetes.NewForConfig(restConfig)
119: 	if err != nil {
120: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create Kubernetes client: %w", err)
121: 	}
122: 
123: 	return &kubeClients{dynamic: client, kube: kubeClient, restConfig: restConfig}, nil
124: }
125: 
126: func (l *clientLoader) load() (*kubeClients, string, error) {
127: 	l.once.Do(func() {
128: 		restConfig, namespace, err := l.loadConfig()
129: 		if err != nil {
130: 			l.err = err
131: 			return
132: 		}
133: 		if namespace == "" {
134: 			namespace = defaultNamespace
135: 		}
136: 
137: 		l.clients, l.err = l.newClients(restConfig)
138: 		l.namespace = namespace
139: 	})
140: 
141: 	return l.clients, l.namespace, l.err
142: }
143: 
144: // connect returns a view of the runtime with its Kubernetes clients populated, loading the
145: // kubeconfig on first use. Every operation that reads or changes cluster state calls it first.
146: func (r *Runtime) connect() (*Runtime, error) {
147: 	if r.connected || r.clients == nil {
148: 		return r, nil
149: 	}
150: 
151: 	clients, namespace, err := r.clients.load()
152: 	if err != nil {
153: 		return nil, err
154: 	}
155: 
156: 	view := *r
157: 	view.client = clients.dynamic
158: 	view.kubeClient = clients.kube
159: 	view.restConfig = clients.restConfig
160: 	if view.namespace == "" {
161: 		view.namespace = namespace
162: 	}
163: 	view.connected = true
164: 
165: 	return &view, nil
166: }
167: 
168: func withKubernetesClientDebugLogs(ctx context.Context) context.Context {
169: 	verbosity := -1
170: 	if log.GetLevel() <= log.DebugLevel {
171: 		verbosity = 3
172: 	}
173: 	logger := funcr.New(func(prefix, args string) {
174: 		log.Debug("Kubernetes client", "log", strings.TrimSpace(prefix+" "+args))
175: 	}, funcr.Options{Verbosity: verbosity})
176: 
177: 	return klog.NewContext(ctx, logger)
178: }
179: 
180: func init() {
181: 	clablabruntime.Register(clablabruntime.ClabernetesRuntimeName, New)
182: }
183: 
184: // New returns the c9s lab runtime. It does not load the kubeconfig: the Kubernetes clients
185: // are created on the first operation that needs the cluster.
186: func New(cfg clablabruntime.Config) (clablabruntime.LabRuntime, error) {
187: 	return &Runtime{
188: 		labNamespaceOverride: configuredLabNamespace(cfg.Namespace),
189: 		timeout:              cfg.Timeout,
190: 		kindLinkApplyMode:    cfg.KindLinkApplyMode,
191: 		clients:              newClientLoader(),
192: 	}, nil
193: }

256: // getShortestTopologyPath calculates the relative path to the provided topology file from
257: // the current working directory and returns it if it is shorted than the absolute path p.
258: func getShortestTopologyPath(p string) (string, error) {
259: 	if p == "" {
260: 		return "", nil
261: 	}
262: 	if strings.Contains(p, "://") {
263: 		return p, nil
264: 	}
265: 
266: 	// get topo file path relative of the cwd
267: 	cwd, err := os.Getwd()
268: 	if err != nil {
269: 		return "", err
270: 	}
271: 
272: 	relPath, err := filepath.Rel(cwd, p)
273: 	if err != nil {
274: 		return "", err
275: 	}
276: 
277: 	if len(relPath) < len(p) {
278: 		return relPath, nil
279: 	}
280: 
281: 	return p, nil
282: }

288: 	sort.Slice(containers, func(i, j int) bool {
289: 		labNameI := containers[i].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
290: 		labNameJ := containers[j].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
291: 
292: 		if labNameI == labNameJ {
293: 			// Use the first name if available
294: 			nameI := ""
295: 			if len(containers[i].Names) > 0 {
296: 				nameI = containers[i].Names[0]
297: 			}
298: 
299: 			nameJ := ""
300: 			if len(containers[j].Names) > 0 {
301: 				nameJ = containers[j].Names[0]
302: 			}
303: 
304: 			return nameI < nameJ
305: 		}
306: 
307: 		return labNameI < labNameJ
308: 	})
309: 
310: 	// Group the sorted containers
311: 	for idx := range containers {
312: 		labName := containers[idx].Labels[clabconstants.Containerlab]
313: 		// Ensure labName exists, default to a placeholder if missing
314: 		// (shouldn't happen with filters)

316: 			labName = "_unknown_lab_"
317: 		}
318: 
319: 		groupedDetails[labName] = append(groupedDetails[labName], containers[idx])

324: 		return fmt.Errorf("failed to marshal grouped container details: %v", err)

Reasoning
The state.go code looks fine. Note: in `enrichState`, the pod enrichment loop: `pod := podsByNode[primary]; if pod == nil { continue }` — a node that has its own pod (in podsByNode[nodeName]) but whose primary has no pod gets skipped. But if primary == nodeName (normal case), primary is the node itself, so pod exists if it exists. Only in a network-mode group where the primary pod is missing but the member's pod exists would this skip — edge case; but for network-mode container, the member shares the primary's pod; if primary pod is missing, there'd likely be no pod for member either. Minor.

Now, let me check the `pollInterfaces` in iface_stats.go head — I only saw the diff hunks. Let me read the head file in full to verify correctness of the new logic (it was heavily rewritten in this PR).

Reasoning
A few observations on iface_stats.go:

1. `processSample`: when an interface disappears, it emits the notpresent event and `delete(tracked.ifaces, name)` — but note it modifies `tracked.ifaces` while iterating over it (the `for name, iface := range tracked.ifaces` loop deletes entries — deleting during range is allowed in Go). Fine.

2. `round`: `poller.round(ctx)` runs synchronously first, then ticker. If `labStates` errors, it returns and skips `retireStoppedNodes`. Fine.

3. Potential issue: `retireStoppedNodes` emits events for ifaces that were tracked as down already (action "down", operstate e.g. "down") — when a node stops, it re-emits "notpresent" for each tracked iface. That's intended per the comment.

4. `sampleAll`: `sem <- struct{}{}` acquired before spawning goroutine; bounded. `samples[idx]` written by goroutine, read after wg.Wait — safe.

5. `p.nodes` — trackedNode keyed by namespace/lab/node. Note that in `round`, `running` map and retireStoppedNodes run after processing; if labStates returns error (e.g., lab not found → nil), fine.

6. Concern: events channel capacity 128 with 4-5 goroutines sending. `sendEvent` — check implementation; if it blocks on a full channel, goroutines could block forever if the consumer is gone... but consumer is Stream loop which exits only on ctx done or error. If consumer returns error while pollers still block on full channel → goroutine leak until process exit. sendEvent presumably uses select with ctx.Done. Let me check sendEvent (events.go:422).

Also `watchTopologies`/`watchNodes`/`watchPods` — on watch error retry loop with backoff? Let me read the rest of events.go (141-438).

Reasoning
`Offline bool` default false (unless config file sets it; viper `IsSet` check handles config). Good.

Now the key remaining question: does `streamLabRuntimeEvents` correctly scope when `--name` is given but no topo? `labRuntimeEventStreamRequest(clab.Config.Name, opts)` — `clab.Config.Name` is set from `o.Global.TopologyName`? Let's check `ToClabOptions` and how Config.Name is populated when only `--name` given. In containerlab, `NewContainerLab` with `--name` sets `c.Config.Name` via option (WithLabNameOnly). Check core/options.

25: func TestContainerFromLabNodeReportsWorkload(t *testing.T) {
26: 	t.Parallel()
27: 
28: 	c := &CLab{Config: &Config{Name: "lab1"}, TopoPaths: &clabtypes.TopoPaths{}}
29: 	ports := []clablabruntime.ExposedPort{{Port: 22, ExposePort: 22, Protocol: "tcp"}}
30: 
31: 	container := c.containerFromLabNode(
32: 		&clablabruntime.LabState{Name: "lab1", Namespace: "c9s-lab1"},
33: 		clablabruntime.NodeState{
34: 			Name:                "r1",
35: 			Pod:                 "lab1-r1-abc",
36: 			Container:           "node-r1-x",
37: 			NodeUID:             "uid-1",
38: 			ExposedPorts:        ports,
39: 			LoadBalancerAddress: "192.0.2.10",
40: 		},
41: 	)
42: 
43: 	if container.ID != "c9s-lab1/lab1/r1" || container.ShortID != container.ID {
44: 		t.Fatalf("ID = %q, ShortID = %q; want the unique <namespace>/<lab>/<node> id",
45: 			container.ID, container.ShortID)
46: 	}
47: 	w := container.Workload
48: 	if w == nil || w.Namespace != "c9s-lab1" || w.Pod != "lab1-r1-abc" ||
49: 		w.Container != "node-r1-x" || w.NodeUID != "uid-1" ||
50: 		w.LoadBalancerAddress != "192.0.2.10" || len(w.ExposedPorts) != 1 {
51: 		t.Fatalf("workload = %+v", w)
52: 	}
53: 
54: 	other := c.containerFromLabNode(
55: 		&clablabruntime.LabState{Name: "lab1", Namespace: "c9s-lab1"},
56: 		clablabruntime.NodeState{Name: "r2"},
57: 	)
58: 	if other.ShortID == container.ShortID {
59: 		t.Fatal("two nodes share a container ID")
60: 	}
61: }

63: func TestDestroyWithLabRuntimePassesCleanup(t *testing.T) {
64: 	t.Parallel()
65: 
66: 	for _, cleanup := range []bool{false, true} {
67: 		runtime := &recordingDestroyLabRuntime{}

577: +		t.Fatalf("ID = %q, ShortID = %q; want the unique <namespace>/<lab>/<node> id",
578: +			container.ID, container.ShortID)
579: +	}

583: +		w.LoadBalancerAddress != "192.0.2.10" || len(w.ExposedPorts) != 1 {

657:  
658:  The local `--cleanup | -c` flag instructs containerlab to remove the lab directory and all its content.
659:  
660:  Without this flag present, containerlab will keep the lab directory and all files inside of it.
661:  
662: +With `--runtime c9s`, `--cleanup` also deletes the lab's persistent node storage (the PersistentVolumeClaims holding saved device configuration) and then the lab namespace. A plain destroy keeps the claims, so the next deploy of the lab boots from the saved configuration. See [device state persistence](../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#device-state-persistence).
663: +
664:  Refer to the [configuration artifacts](../manual/conf-artifacts.md) page to get more information on the lab directory contents.
665:  
666:  #### graceful
667:  
668:  To make containerlab attempt a graceful shutdown of the running containers, add the `--graceful` flag to destroy cmd. Without it, containers will be removed forcefully without even attempting to stop them.

673: @@ -75,12 +75,16 @@ Currently supported runtimes:
674:  
675:  - `docker`
676:  - `c9s`
677:  
678:  With `--runtime c9s`, events are backed by kubernetes watches for Clabernetes
679: -`Topology` resources and labeled Pods. Interface statistics are sampled inside
680: -the device containers, not through local host netlink.
681: +`Topology` and `Node` resources and labeled Pods. Interface state (`interface up`
682: +and `interface down` events) and statistics are sampled inside the device
683: +containers, not through local host netlink. The stream covers every namespace by
684: +default; `--namespace` (or `CLAB_KUBE_NAMESPACE`) limits it to one namespace,
685: +and `-t`/`--name` to one lab. With Docker and Podman the lab selection is ignored
686: +and every lab is streamed.
687:  
688:  Runtimes that do not implement the `events` API, or are not yet supported by Containerlab, will exit with an explanatory error.
689:

702: +/// note | Lab runtimes
703: +With a lab runtime such as `--runtime c9s`, `graph` renders from the topology file alone: `--mermaid`, `--dot`, `--drawio` and the HTML server with `--offline` work, and need no cluster access. The default HTML mode, which reads the running containers, and `--node-filter` are rejected. `--drawio` still runs the clab-io-draw container on the local host.
704: +///
705: +
706:  ### HTML
707:  
708:  The HTML-based graph representation is the default graphing option. The topology will be graphed and served online using the embedded web server.
709:  
710:  The default graph template is based on the NeXt UI framework[^2].

720:  /// note | Clabernetes runtime
721: -With `--runtime c9s`, `inspect` reads Clabernetes `Topology` resources and their related kubernetes objects instead of local Docker containers. `inspect --all` lists c9s topologies across all namespaces. See [Containerlab runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#inspect) for details.
722: +With `--runtime c9s`, `inspect` reads Clabernetes `Topology` resources and their related kubernetes objects instead of local Docker containers. `inspect --all` lists c9s topologies across all namespaces, or in the `--namespace` override. The JSON output uses `<namespace>/<lab>/<node>` as `container_id` and adds the `namespace`, `pod`, `container`, `node_uid`, `exposed_ports` and `load_balancer_address` fields. See [Containerlab runtime](../../manual/clabernetes/runtime.md#inspect) for details.
723:  ///
724:  
725:  ### Usage

727:  `containerlab [global-flags] inspect [local-flags]`

# Review: Lab runtime command support, workload inspection, event scoping, and claim cleanup

## Summary

This PR integrates lab-runtime (c9s/clabernetes) semantics across the CLI surface: `graph` now supports topology-file-only modes under lab runtimes, `inspect` JSON gains a `LabRuntimeWorkload` block with a unique `<namespace>/<lab>/<node>` container ID, `events` gains lab/namespace scoping, destroy/reconfigure plumb `Cleanup` through to the runtime, and `CheckConnectivity` short-circuits for lab runtimes. The implementation is small, focused, and consistently documented; the three new test files cover the introduced behavior directly.

I found no blocking defects. The design choices I probed — the `connect()` idempotence pattern, event channel backpressure, `noShell` caching, pod selection, flag-detection fallbacks, and nil-embedded-pointer JSON behavior — each have correct guards or intentional, documented tradeoffs.

## Findings

No actionable findings were identified in this revision.

## Coverage notes

- **Scope**: All 31 changed paths from `/source/manifest.json` were reviewed via `/source/diff.txt` (read in full) plus head files under `/source/head` and base files under `/source/base` for comparison.
- **Verification limitation**: This is a static, source-only review. Tests were not executed and no cluster or container environment was available; the pass/fail of the new tests (`cmd/labruntime_gaps_test.go`, `core/labruntime_gaps_test.go`, `core/events/labruntime_test.go`) was assessed by inspection only.
- **Checks performed**:
  - `cmd/root.go`: `checkLabRuntimeCommandSupport` ordering in `preRunFn`, the `graphTopologyFileFlags` / `labRuntimeUnsupportedFlags` contract, and the `labRuntimeFlagWasSet` viper fallback (pre-existing helper, correctly reused).
  - `cmd/graph.go` and `core/config.go`: the `LoadTopologyNodes` split from `parseTopology`, including the lab-runtime early `break` in the runtime-init loop and the no-nodes edge case.
  - `labruntime/clabernetes`: every exported cluster-touching method calls `connect()`; `Validate`/`Manifests` are intentionally offline; `clientLoader.once` makes concurrent connect safe.
  - `events.go` / `state.go` / `iface_stats.go`: channel capacities with ctx-aware non-blocking sends, `newestPod` selection, `podsByNode` guard, `noShell` mutex discipline and pod-name keying, worker-pool semaphore bounds, and `retireStoppedNodes` dedup behavior.
  - `cmd/inspect.go` + `types/types.go`: nil-embedded-pointer JSON omission verified against the new test's docker-record assertions.
  - `core/events/stream.go` + `cmd/events.go`: lab-runtime vs local-runtime stream split; the docs claim that Docker/Podman ignore lab selection matches the implementation (no name filter in the local path).
  - Docs: `destroy.md` (claim retention on plain destroy), `events.md` (scoping), `graph.md` (topology-file-only modes), `inspect/index.md` (new JSON fields), and `runtime.md` (reconfigure deleting persistent storage, lines 353/381/772) all match implemented behavior.
